subject: Post-call: Aurea Financial — PII & Logging Requirements + Next Steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@aureafin.com>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@aureafin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:08:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Aurea Financial — PII & Logging Requirements + Next Steps

Hi Elena / Marcus —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please reply if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Customer-facing LLM endpoints currently inject or surface PII in logs, creating audit and compliance risk.
- Security team requires no raw PII in persistent logs; any PII must be redacted at ingestion or never written to disk.
- Retention policy complexity: operational logs need short retention (30–90 days) while audit trails/meta must be retained for up to 7 years for regulatory audits.
- Need for exportable, tamper-evident audit logs (CSV/JSON) for external auditors and internal compliance reviews.
- Desire to avoid sending degraded telemetry to third-party SaaS analytics without explicit redaction/encryption guarantees.

Current stack you shared:
- API layer + request logging to an in-house telemetry pipeline that lands in Snowflake.
- Datadog for short-term metrics and alerts.
- Key management via AWS KMS; roadmap includes an HSM evaluation.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Redwood must provide (or operate inside) a configuration that prevents raw PII from being persisted in logs by default.
- Ability to support configurable retention windows per log class (e.g., full request traces 30–90d, redaction hashes and audit metadata 7y).
- Exportable audit package for attestation and SOC2-type evidence, including append-only change history.
- Deployment options that meet your network controls (VPC Private + customer KMS or on-prem bundle).

Questions / clarifications I have for the security team (we'll coordinate):
- Can you confirm the set of fields you consider PII for this integration (names, emails, account IDs, payment tokens, free-text)?
- Do you need deterministic hashes of PII in logs, or strictly irreversible redaction?
- Any constraints on how long redaction/erasure requests must be actionable (e.g., within 48 hours)?

Proposed next steps (action owners & timing):
1) Naomi (Redwood) to share SOC2 summary + pen test highlights and our redaction design document — EOD 11/15 (attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).
2) Aurea security deep-dive (technical) with Rishi and Monica — target 11/18 (60m).
3) Redwood to provide a mutual action plan (MAP) + draft SOW that enumerates retention windows and export deliverables — draft 11/19 (attached template: aurea-mpa-draft.xlsx).
4) If technical fit, schedule a short Private deployment demo (VPC + KMS flow) and sample audit export — week of 11/22.

If that aligns, Elena / Marcus can confirm availability for the 11/18 slot and send the PII-field list so Rishi can prepare the redaction options we'll propose.

Thanks again — appreciated the transparency on regulatory needs. I know this is sensitive and we want to make the integration as automatable as possible while preserving your auditability.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Naomi —

This captures the conversation well. A few quick clarifications from my side:
- PII scope: full name, email, phone, SSN, payment token, and any free-text that contains personally identifying statements.
- We prefer irreversible redaction for logs, but we need an option for deterministic salted hashing for audit metadata (so we can correlate events without revealing raw values).
- Erasure requests: security wants the ability to flag and expunge any specific session trace within 72 hours, and to verify deletion for auditors.

We're available 11/18 10:00–12:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Marcus will share the PII fields list and a short compliance checklist before then.

Thanks — looking forward to the SOC2 + redaction notes.

—Elena
Elena Rodriguez
Director, Data Security | Aurea Financial

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Aurea prep: tasks for the 11/18 deep-dive

Rishi / Monica —

Aurea confirmed 11/18 10:00–11:00 PT for the technical session. Per the email thread (below) they want:
- Overview of our redaction strategies: irreversible redaction vs salted deterministic hashes; include performance/latency impact and examples.
- Pattern-based ingestion redaction + custom field rules mapping to their PII definition.
- Retention configuration UI and how to enforce multi-tier windows (30/90 days vs 7 years for metadata).
- Exportable audit bundle: show CSV/JSON export and tamper-evidence (checksum/versioned exports).
- KMS options: customer-managed KMS flow in VPC + on-prem alternatives.

Action items:
- Rishi: prepare a short runbook (1–2 slides) showing where redaction occurs (edge vs gateway vs store) and latency numbers for each.
- Monica: assemble a sample export package and a short script that generates the audit CSV for a synthetic session.
- Naomi: I'll attach the SOC2 summary and our redaction-design note to the HubSpot deal and send the MAP draft to Aurea after the call.

Please keep slides tight — 20 minutes for us to present, 40 for live Q&A.

Thanks — Naomi
